title: Lenia specialist predator persistence vs arena size, five sizes x 2 seeds: 80-120 t at 160-192^2, a split at 224^2 (250 t vs alive at 1200 t), 710-940 t at 256^2, alive at 1200 t at 320^2: a threshold near 224^2 rather than a smooth law
summary: Same world and parameters as 20261026T0003-c26-lenia-predator-arena (world.py there, WORLD_P {"PRED":1,"T_INTRO":200,"PSIG":8,"DECB":0.002,"DOMAIN":L}, runle.py counts every 10 t), adding 192^2 and 224^2 on seeds 1 and 2 to t=1400 (data/). Predator persistence after its introduction at t=200 (last time with >= 1 predator cell): 160^2 80 and 100 (runs to t=800); 192^2 90 and 120; 224^2 250 (seed 1) and still alive at t=1400 with five prey-predator cycles of period ~250-300 t (seed 2); 256^2 940 and 710 (runs to 1200); 320^2 alive at t=1400 on both seeds. So persistence jumps between 192^2 and 256^2, with 224^2 split between seeds, which looks like a critical arena size (about 1.9-2x the 160^2 area) more than a smooth exponential. With the predator gone, prey saturate at 47-50 (192^2) and 69 (224^2) cells.

finding.operator: predation (matter transfer from prey to predator) between two Lenia replicator species
finding.control: arena size 160/192/224/256/320 at fixed parameters, seeds 1 and 2

limits: Two seeds per size, so the 224^2 split is a coin flip, not a probability; runs are censored at t=1400 (t=800 at 160^2, 1200 at 256^2), so the long-lived arms may still go extinct later. One parameter set. Not yet a law: the question's held-out-size prediction was not made.
